Exact contextual exception: onboarding.personalGoal.validation uses 'רווחים' to mean whitespace/spaces, not profits; term_audit.py has no per-key exception field, so review that hit by meaning rather than weakening the forbidden list.

minute_unit.note: Apple he abbreviates minutes as 'דק׳' with U+05F3 geresh (iOS 26.1 (23B86), HealthUI and Activity strings). Keep a space between the count and unit. Apple's '%@ min' sample includes U+200F, but a leading number does not require that mark in every app view; inspect the rendered line and add only a tested local fix. Spoken strings use 'דקות'.

screen_time.note: Apple's he name for the feature (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Screen Time; System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | ScreenTimeControllerTitle). Apple writes the feature name inside gershayim when it names it in a sentence, '‏״%@״ מבקש גישה ל״זמן מסך״' (Applications/FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_TITLE), so the mock alert keys reproduce the quotes and the bidi marks verbatim. Generic hours-on-screen is a different concept and takes plain wording, which the forms list cannot distinguish: a hit inside insights.savings.estimateExplanation or screenTimeReport.noDataExplanation is read by a human, not by the count.

Prefer a clear verbal noun for a short action, an infinitive for a step, same-written past forms for achievements and informal plural selectively in longer direct copy; impersonal frames are a fallback when they read naturally. Choose controls by role and effect, not a universal grammar rule. Record any unavoidable masculine-singular key. The existing he catalog units remain needs_review.
